rounds.text: Nazara Technologies Ltd demonstrates exceptional compounding capabilities, evidenced by a 5-year profit growth CAGR of 155% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 116% [E19, E21]. This explosive earnings momentum is backed by healthy operational efficiency, featuring a 5-year median return on equity of 13% that scales up to 31% over the last year [E26, E28], alongside a strong 27.1% ROCE [E12]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt free with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x as of September 2026 [E36, E58], and its robust cash generation is highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs 149 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of 1.82x for March 2026 [E33, E34]. The market structure also reflects high internal confidence, with promoter holding expanding significantly by 15.56 percentage points to 31.99% by October 2026 [E40], and the equity scoring a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 while trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E49, E50]. Conceded: [E1] Trades at an elevated P/E of 1246x, and [E44] a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 17 per share against a market price of Rs 410.

Nazara Technologies Ltd carries extreme valuation risks that are entirely disconnected from operational reality, trading at an astronomical P/E ratio of 1246x against a sector benchmark of 16.22x [E1, E6]. This exorbitant pricing is underscored by a discounted cash flow model indicating an intrinsic value of Rs 17 per share against a market price of Rs 410, leaving a severe margin of safety of -2317.0% [E44, E45]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF reveals that the current market price already bakes in an unrealistic 66.5% earnings growth rate, vastly eclipsing the base case expectation of 18.0% [E46]. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has actually contracted by -2%, signalling a cooling top line that fails to justify such aggressive valuation multiples [E17]. Institutional confidence is visibly faltering as domestic institutions slashed their holdings from 16.80% in March 2024 to 2.75% in October 2026, accompanied by negative money flow signals [E42, E43], while promoters have encumbered 87.7% of their total holdings [E67]. Conceded: the company delivers strong long-term profit growth of 155% CAGR over five years, maintains a clean balance sheet with low debt, and exhibits robust cash generation where profits are fully backed by operating cash flows [E19, E36, E33, E58].

Conceded: the P/E ratio is 1246x and the discounted cash flow model suggests a low intrinsic value [E1, E44]. However, focusing solely on static valuation metrics ignores the explosive fundamental turnaround currently underway, demonstrated by a quarterly operating margin of 11% in September 2026 compared to -31% in the year-ago quarter [E30]. The business is translating these accelerating operations into tangible cash, achieving a cash conversion ratio of 1.82x with operating cash flow reaching Rs 149 Cr for March 2026 [E33, E34]. Furthermore, long-term profit growth of 155% CAGR over 5 years and 194% over 3 years proves the company's historical capacity to massively outpace base expectations [E19, E20]. While domestic institutional holdings decreased, promoters and foreign institutions actively increased their stakes to 31.99% and 15.42% respectively as of October 2026 [E40, E41]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the company an 84 out of 100 score supported by a 203% year-on-year net profit surge, validating the strength of the underlying asset beyond isolated model outputs [E68, E71].

Conceded: quarterly operating margin reached 11% in September 2026 and net profit surged 203% year-on-year [E30, E71]. However, pointing to these short-term expansions ignores the broader valuation reality where the stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 1246x and a P/B of 4.12x [E1, E2]. The bull cites historical profit growth of 155% over 5 years [E19], but this fails to justify a reverse DCF implying 66.5% ongoing earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E46]. Furthermore, while the bull highlights increased promoter stake at 31.99% [E40], it omits the critical governance warning that promoters have pledged 87.7% of their holding [E67]. The bull values foreign institutional accumulation [E41], yet domestic institutional holdings dropped significantly to 2.75% alongside overall negative money flow [E42, E43]. Finally, relying on a rules-based screen score of 84 [E68] glosses over the inherent valuation blind spot where intrinsic value models output a severe overvaluation warning [E73, E75].

Conceded: [E67] regarding pledged promoter shares. However, dismissing the explosive quarterly operating margin expansion to 11% and the 203% year-on-year net profit surge misses the core operational momentum that is actively materializing [E30, E71]. The critique of the 1246x P/E and 4.12x P/B [E1, E2] ignores the reality that fundamentals are currently outpacing stock price appreciation, demonstrated by a 155% 5-year profit CAGR compared to only 7% 5-year price growth [E19, E22, E55]. While the bear highlights domestic institutional liquidation and negative money flow [E42, E43], it glosses over the substantial counter-flow of foreign institutions increasing their stake to 15.42% alongside a surging promoter commitment now resting at 31.99% [E40, E41]. Furthermore, leaning heavily on static DCF models [E46, E73] undervalues a business generating 1.82x cash conversion with Rs 149 Cr in operating cash flow, Rs 36 Cr in free cash flow, and a robust rules-based screen score of 84 [E33, E34, E35, E68].

The bull’s reliance on quarterly margin expansion [E30] ignores that the yearly operating-margin trend remains inconsistent [E31], suggesting that the recent spike may be a transient fluctuation rather than a sustainable operational shift. While the bull highlights profit growth [E19, E71], it fails to address that the company’s return on assets (0.24%) and return on equity (0.35%) are drastically lower than sector benchmarks [E8, E9], indicating that these profits are not being generated efficiently. Conceded: the company has increased its promoter and foreign institutional holdings [E40, E41]. However, this does not mitigate the risk posed by the fact that 87.7% of promoter holdings are currently pledged [E67], a significant red flag for long-term stability. Furthermore, the bull’s dismissal of the DCF model [E46, E73] ignores that the current market price already demands an unrealistic 66.5% earnings growth rate to justify its valuation [E46]. Finally, the bull cites cash conversion [E33] but overlooks that the company’s compounded sales growth has turned negative at -2% over the trailing twelve months [E17], casting doubt on the long-term viability of the growth narrative.
